A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OrbitZoo. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and extensive appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original RL mission experiments, computational scaling measurements, and analyses comparing simulated trajectories with Starlink ephemerides.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and Starlink results and adds DDPG transfer experiments, DDQN collision-avoidance results, and federated-learning evaluations.

M1.justification: Orekit's PropagatorsParallelizer and federated learning are future work in v1 Appendices C.3 and D.5. v2 implements configurable sequential/parallel propagation and adds GEO training with FedAvg aggregation of locally trained critics (Appendices D.3 and E.6). These are substantive procedural additions, while the underlying Body/Satellite/PettingZoo architecture remains.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix E.2 adds a Kolosa-inspired low-thrust transfer requiring simultaneous changes to several orbital elements, extending the existing Hohmann and moving-target transfer coverage. The collision-avoidance, GEO coordination, and Starlink validation domains remain; no new real satellite dataset is reported.

E2.justification: The PPO-only mission evaluations expand to DDQN versus PPO for collision avoidance and independent versus FedAvg-based PPO for GEO coordination (v2 Appendices E.5–E.6). Appendix E.2 also introduces a Kolosa-inspired reproduction and qualitative comparison with the published implementation, explicitly acknowledging implementation differences.

E3.justification: Reported chase-target steps change from 70 to 500 seconds. GEO episodes change from 2000 to 500 steps, with revised learning rates, epochs, clipping, and update budgets; the new comparison uses matched initial constellations. Hohmann initial action standard deviation changes from 0.4 to 0.5. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing that every retained plot was regenerated.

E4.justification: v2 adds learning-speed and fuel analyses to the existing Hohmann reward-shaping comparison, examines DDQN robustness to realistic perturbations, and tests knowledge sharing in GEO coordination. Parallelization analysis now compares computation modes across force configurations. Conversely, v1's four-day collision-avoidance stress test and associated failure evidence are removed.

E5.justification: v2 Figures 10–11 add ±1 standard-deviation bands to timing measurements, retaining the stated 100 propagation steps. GEO evaluation still reports thirty Monte Carlo simulations, but v2 Figure 29 shows averages without the individual trial traces displayed in v1 Figure 21. No increased run count or new training-seed reporting is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds DDPG learning results, DDQN collision-avoidance outcomes, and federated GEO results. Its collision comparison reports roughly 40 km of semi-major-axis reduction for DDQN versus a roughly 3 km increase for PPO under realistic dynamics. Timing and GEO comparisons are replaced under revised conditions, and four-day collision results disappear. Starlink Table 2 remains 24.14, 83.75, and 1924.90 meters.

T1.justification: v2 substantially expands the formal material with a Jacobian/state-transition derivation of covariance propagation, explicit equinoctial transformations, DDQN and DDPG objectives and updates, and weighted FedAvg aggregation with an IID convergence assumption (Appendices B–C). v1 supplies orbital mechanics and PPO/GAE mathematics but lacks these additional formulations. No new theorem or proof is presented.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a customizable, high-fidelity orbital RL environment, and the abstract's 0.16% MAPE claim is unchanged. v2 adds prominent claims about fast parallel scaling, concludes that continuous action spaces generally improve performance under realistic dynamics, and extends the platform's stated relevance to broader autonomy research.

C2.justification: v2 makes parallelization benefits conditional on force complexity and adds substantive mission-specific limitations: stochastic precision problems in Hohmann transfers, inclination-related chase failures, collision-policy generalization difficulties, and slow or unstable GEO coordination. It also attributes advantages to continuous control and federated knowledge sharing. These extend the scientific interpretation beyond relocating v1's existing caveats.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an explicit experiment-code repository link, DDPG/DDQN architectures and replay settings, a discrete collision-action table, and previously unspecified numerical reward weights across missions. It also documents the propagation-mode configuration. These materially expand reproducibility information; newly disclosed reward coefficients do not themselves establish changed objectives.

R1.justification: Related work and Table 1 expand to additional halo-orbit station-keeping, graph-based multi-agent collision avoidance, and cooperative formation-flying research. New discussions connect OrbitZoo to federated learning, multi-objective RL, and constrained or safety-critical learning. This broadens research positioning substantially beyond reference renumbering or the Armando-to-Herrera name correction.

P1.justification: The former framework section moves to Appendix A, while a new main Section 4 organizes the narrative around RL research challenges. Background passages are extensively rewritten, experiments receive standardized setup and limitations subsections, and the impact statement moves into an expanded final appendix. These are substantial structural and explanatory revisions.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and figure placement, relocates and redraws the architecture/interface displays, and switches screenshots to light backgrounds. It adds algorithm/action tables and learning/comparison plots, redesigns the parallelization and GEO figures, and removes the four-day collision display. Many Starlink plots are retained and merely relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited comparative evaluation and missing reproduction details through DDQN–PPO and independent–federated comparisons, explicit reward and implementation specifications, and an experiment-code link. Its revised parallelization analysis and more specific failure discussions also make the benchmark easier to assess. Removing the four-day collision stress test and replacing GEO trial traces with means reduces some diagnostic evidence, but these losses do not outweigh the gains in empirical support and reproducibility. Changed protocols preclude claiming a general same-setting performance improvement.
